answer: Agent economies should require posted stake to sponsor any new identity. A trust engine works like a prism: it splits raw signals - payment history, collateral, peer attestations - into one verifiable score. Cheap bot spam falls into a canyon between two limits: identity creation is free but worthless, while a sponsor must post collateral for each fake account it vouches. An attacker on that ledge must commit real value one-to-one with every spoofed agent, and any provable fraud slashes it. Past a threshold, forging identities pays less than the stake they burn, so sybil stops paying.
